cases.heading: False or Misleading Risk Presentation
cases.claim: “2.5mg/mL provides easy dose titration as body surface area-based dosing is recommended.”
cases.context: Email includes Boxed Warning but omits all other W&P, including Risk of Improper Dosing (once-weekly dosing; mistaken daily use led to fatal toxicity; household teaspoon not accurate). Links to full PI do not mitigate.
cases.rationale: Omitting W&P, especially improper-dosing risk tied to the dosing claim, suggests the drug is safer than demonstrated.
cases.check: Rule: all W&P must be represented in pieces with benefit claims; dosing claims must be accompanied by related dosing-error warnings.

cases.cat: Lack of fair balance (risk presentation prominence)
cases.heading: False or Misleading Risk Presentation
cases.claim: Benefit claims presented in the email body as a bulleted list; the Boxed Warning is presented after the signature block.
cases.context: Signature block typically signals end of correspondence.
cases.rationale: Risk not presented with comparable prominence and readability.
cases.check: Rule: in emails, flag risk/ISI placed after the signature block or sign-off.

cases.cat: Broadening of indication / omission of material indication information
cases.heading: False or Misleading Benefit Presentation
cases.claim: “I wanted to let you know that Xatmep® (methotrexate) oral solution is available for your patients with Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia.”
cases.context: Indication is pediatric ALL as part of a multi-phase combination chemotherapy maintenance regimen; full indication only after signature block.
cases.rationale: Implies use in all ages and without combination therapy.
cases.check: Rule: indication mentions must include population (pediatric) and regimen qualifiers (combination maintenance) from the PI.
